questions.question: Acyclic alkanes have which general formula?
questions.explanation: Acyclic alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.question: Which hybridization is found on each carbon atom of an alkane?
questions.explanation: Each carbon atom in an alkane has sp3 hybrid orbitals.

questions.question: Markovnikov addition places hydrogen on which alkene carbon?
questions.explanation: Markovnikov addition places hydrogen on the carbon that already has more hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: Terminal alkynes contain which acidic atom?
questions.explanation: Terminal alkynes contain an acidic hydrogen attached to the triple bond carbon.

questions.question: Catalytic hydrogenation of alkenes uses which catalyst?
questions.explanation: Nickel, platinum, or palladium catalyzes alkene hydrogenation.

questions.question: Alkyl halides contain a halogen bonded to which carbon type?
questions.explanation: Alkyl halides have a halogen covalently bonded to an sp3 hybridized carbon.

questions.question: A tertiary alkyl halide has the halogen attached to a carbon bonded to how many alkyl groups?
questions.explanation: In a tertiary alkyl halide the halogen-bearing carbon is bonded to three alkyl groups.

questions.question: SN2 reaction rate depends on concentrations of which species?
questions.explanation: SN2 is bimolecular and its rate depends on both substrate and nucleophile concentrations.

questions.question: SN1 proceeds through which intermediate?
questions.explanation: SN1 reactions proceed through a carbocation intermediate.

questions.question: E2 requires leaving group and beta hydrogen to be in which arrangement?
questions.explanation: E2 needs an anti periplanar arrangement for optimal orbital overlap.

questions.question: Most stable carbon allotrope at normal conditions is which form?
questions.explanation: alpha graphite is the most stable carbon form at normal temperature and pressure.

questions.question: C60 contains how many pentagonal rings?
questions.explanation: C60 has 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons.

questions.question: Nanotechnology manipulates matter at scales of approximately which range?
questions.explanation: Nanotechnology operates at about 1 to 100 nm in at least one dimension.

questions.question: Carbon nanotubes are rolled sheets of which material?
questions.explanation: CNTs are formed by rolling graphene sheets into tubes.

questions.question: Silicon belongs to which group of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a Group 14 element.

questions.question: The carboxyl functional group consists of a carbonyl group bonded to which group?
questions.explanation: The carboxyl group contains a carbonyl C=O directly bonded to an OH group.

questions.question: Carboxylic acids are named by replacing the terminal -e of the alkane with which suffix?
questions.explanation: IUPAC names for carboxylic acids end with -oic acid.

questions.question: Carboxylic acids are classified as which type of acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids only partially ionize in water, making them weak acids.

questions.question: The reaction of a carboxylic acid and an alcohol with an acid catalyst is called which process?
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed ester formation is known as Fischer esterification.

questions.question: Amides can be reduced by lithium aluminum hydride to give which product?
questions.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces amides to amines.

questions.question: Group 1 elements have which valence configuration?
questions.explanation: Alkali metals have one valence electron in an ns orbital.

questions.question: Sodium metal is extracted by electrolysis of which molten compound?
questions.explanation: Down's process electrolyses molten sodium chloride.

questions.question: Flame test color for sodium is which?
questions.explanation: Sodium gives a yellow flame color.

questions.question: Alkaline earth metals have which valence configuration?
questions.explanation: Group IIA elements have two valence electrons in an ns orbital.

questions.question: Plaster of Paris is formed by heating gypsum to which temperature?
questions.explanation: Heating gypsum at about 120 C gives calcium sulphate hemihydrate.

questions.question: Organic chemistry deals with compounds containing which elements?
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry deals with compounds containing carbon, hydrogen, and other non-metal elements.

questions.question: Wohler synthesized urea in which year?
questions.explanation: Wohler synthesized urea in 1828.

questions.question: August Kekulé proposed the theory of what type of carbon?
questions.explanation: Kekulé proposed the theory of tetravalent carbon.

questions.question: Biochemistry combines organic chemistry with which field?
questions.explanation: Biochemistry combines organic chemistry with biology.

questions.question: Berzelius proposed which theory regarding carbon compounds?
questions.explanation: Berzelius proposed the vital force theory.

questions.question: Molecularity refers to the number of what in a step?
questions.explanation: Molecularity is the number of species that must collide to produce the reaction indicated by that step.

questions.question: A termolecular reaction involves how many reactant molecules?
questions.explanation: A termolecular reaction requires the collision of three reactant molecules.

questions.question: The slowest step in a reaction mechanism is called which?
questions.explanation: In multiple-step reactions, the slowest step determines the rate and is called the rate-determining step.

questions.question: The Arrhenius equation relates rate constant to which two factors?
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation expresses the dependence of the rate constant on absolute temperature and activation energy.

questions.question: A catalyst that is present in the same phase as reactants is called which?
questions.explanation: A homogeneous catalyst is present in the same phase as the reacting molecules.

questions.question: Elements in the d-block are referred to as which type of transition elements?
questions.explanation: The d-block elements are referred to as Outer Transition Elements.

questions.question: The main ore of Titanium is which mineral?
questions.explanation: Ilmenite is the main ore of Titanium.

questions.question: Haematite is an ore of Iron with which formula?
questions.explanation: Haematite is alpha-Fe2O3.

questions.question: Cobalt occurs as which ore?
questions.explanation: Cobalt occurs as Cobaltite.

questions.question: Zinc blende is also known as which mineral?
questions.explanation: Zinc blende is also known as Sphalerite.

questions.question: Transition metals are found in which block of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Transition metals are located in the d-block, groups 3 through 12.

questions.question: When transition metals form cations they lose which electrons first?
questions.explanation: Transition metals lose their ns electrons first when forming ions.

questions.question: A molecule or ion that donates an electron pair to a metal is called which?
questions.explanation: Ligands donate electron pairs to the central metal to form coordinate bonds.

questions.question: A low spin complex forms when the splitting energy is which?
questions.explanation: Low spin occurs when the crystal field splitting energy exceeds the pairing energy.

questions.question: Iron is used as a catalyst in which industrial process?
questions.explanation: Iron catalyzes the Haber process for ammonia synthesis.

questions.question: Normal alkanes from C1 to C4 are in which physical state at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Normal alkanes with one to four carbons are colourless gases.

questions.question: Lucas Test gives immediate turbidity with which alcohol class?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react fastest with Lucas reagent and give immediate turbidity.

questions.question: Heterogeneous catalysis occurs when catalyst and reactants are in which arrangement?
questions.explanation: In heterogeneous catalysis, the catalyst exists in a different phase from the reacting species.

questions.question: Which derivative of carboxylic acid is the most reactive?
questions.explanation: Acid chlorides are the most reactive of the common carboxylic acid derivatives.

questions.question: Hemoglobin contains which transition metal?
questions.explanation: Iron is present in the heme group of hemoglobin.
